akhfash:2-2.t: He said ﴿وَأَنتَ حِلٌّ﴾: among the Arabs are those who say "أنتَ حِلٌّ" and "أنتَ حَلال" ("you are out of the state of consecration"), "أَنْتَ حِرْمٌ" and "أَنتَ حَرامٌ" ("you are in the state of consecration"), and "هو المُحِلّ" and "المُحْرِم". [And] you say "أَحْلَلْنا" and "أحْرَمْنا", and you say "حَلَلْنا", which is the good (form).

akhfash:11-11.t: And He said ﴿فَلاَ ٱقتَحَمَ ٱلْعَقَبَةَ﴾: He means ﴿فَلَمْ يَقَتْحِمْ﴾ ("he did not attempt"), as He said ﴿فَلاَ صَدَّقَ﴾, that is: he did not believe (فلم يُصَدِّقْ).

akhfash:13-13.t: And He said ﴿فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ﴾, that is: "the steep path is the freeing of a neck ﴿أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ﴾" (العقبةُ فكُّ رقبةٍ). And some read ﴿فَكَّ رقبةً﴾, and that is not as good; ﴿فكُّ رقبةٍ﴾ is the good (reading).

akhfash:14-15.t: And He said ﴿أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ﴾ ﴿يَتِيماً﴾: "اليتيم" (the orphan) is accusative through "الإِطعام" (the maṣdar, "feeding").

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَأَنْتَ﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿حِلٌّ﴾: lawful ﴿بِهَذَا الْبَلَدِ﴾, in that it will be made lawful for you to fight in it; and Allah fulfilled this promise for him on the day of the Conquest. So the clause is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ) between what is sworn by and what is conjoined to it.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَوَالِدٍ﴾, that is, Ādam, ﴿وَمَا وَلَدَ﴾, that is, his offspring; «ما» is in the sense of «من» ("who").

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ﴾, that is, the species, ﴿فِي كَبَدٍ﴾: toil and hardship; he endures the calamities of this world and the hardships of the Hereafter.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿أَيَحْسَبُ﴾: does he think — man, the strong man of Quraysh, who is Abū al-Ashudd ibn Kilda, because of his strength — ﴿أَنْ﴾: lightened (mukhaffafa) from the heavy «أنّ», its noun being omitted, that is, «أنه» — ﴿لَنْ يَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ أَحَدٌ﴾? But Allah has power over him.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿يَقُولُ أَهْلَكْتُ﴾ in enmity to Muhammad ﴿مَالًا لُبَدًا﴾: abundant, piled one upon another.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿أَيَحْسَبُ أَنْ﴾, that is, «أنه», ﴿لَمْ يَرَهُ أَحَدٌ﴾ in what he spent, so as to know its amount? But Allah knows its amount, and that it is not something to boast of, and He will recompense him for his evil deed.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿أَلَمْ نَجْعَلْ﴾: an interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīr), that is, We made ﴿لَهُ عَيْنَيْنِ﴾

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَلِسَانًا وَشَفَتَيْنِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَهَدَيْنَاهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ﴾: We made clear to him the way of good and of evil.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿فَلَا﴾: so why did he not ﴿اقْتَحَمَ الْعَقَبَةَ﴾: pass over it?

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ﴾ — made you know — ﴿مَا الْعَقَبَةُ﴾ that he should pass over: a magnifying of its matter; and the clause is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ). He made clear the means of crossing it by His words:

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿فَكَّ رَقَبَةً﴾ from slavery, by setting it free,

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿أَوْ أَطْعَمَ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ﴾: famine,

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿أَوْ مِسْكِينًا ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ﴾: clinging to the dust because of his poverty. In one reading [فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ]: in place of the two verbs, two nominative maṣdars (verbal nouns), the first being muḍāf (in a genitive construct) to «رقبة» and the second taking tanwīn; then «اقتحام» is implied before «العقبة», and the reading mentioned is its explanation.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿ثُمَّ كَانَ﴾: conjoined to «اقتحم», and «ثم» is for order in mention (al-tartīb al-dhikrī); the meaning is: he was, at the time of passing over, ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَتَوَاصَوْا﴾: enjoined one another ﴿بِالصَّبْرِ﴾ in obedience and away from disobedience ﴿وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْمَرْحَمَةِ﴾: mercy towards creation.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾ described with these qualities ﴿أَصْحَابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ﴾: the right.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآيَاتِنَا هُمْ أَصْحَابُ الْمَشْأَمَةِ﴾: the left.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ نَارٌ مُؤْصَدَةٌ﴾ — with hamza, and with wāw in its place — closed over.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿لا أُقْسِمُ﴾: لا is redundant (zāʾida), and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿بِهذَا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الْبَلَدِ﴾: badal (substitute); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿وَأَنْتَ حِلٌّ﴾: the wāw is parenthetical, and a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is parenthetical and has no grammatical position; ﴿بِهذَا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them; ﴿الْبَلَدِ﴾: badal (substitute) for the demonstrative.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَوالِدٍ﴾: conjoined to البلد; ﴿وَما﴾: also conjoined to البلد; ﴿وَلَدَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿لَقَدْ﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to the oath and قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿خَلَقْنَا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿الْإِنْسانَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿فِي كَبَدٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿أَيَحْسَبُ﴾: the hamza is a particle of reproachful interrogation, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿أَنْ﴾: lightened from the heavy (anna), its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); ﴿لَنْ يَقْدِرَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by lan; ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿أَحَدٌ﴾: agent; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of an, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of يحسب.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿يَقُولُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَهْلَكْتُ﴾: a past verb and its agent; ﴿مالًا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿لُبَداً﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is the maqūl (speech content) of the saying.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿أَيَحْسَبُ﴾: the hamza is a particle of reproachful interrogation, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿أَنْ﴾: lightened from the heavy (anna), its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); ﴿لَمْ يَرَهُ﴾: an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿أَحَدٌ﴾: agent; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of an, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of يحسب.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿أَلَمْ نَجْعَلْ﴾: the hamza is a particle of affirmative interrogation, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿لَهُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿عَيْنَيْنِ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿وَلِساناً وَشَفَتَيْنِ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿وَهَدَيْناهُ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿النَّجْدَيْنِ﴾: its second object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿فَلَا﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle and لا is negative; ﴿اقْتَحَمَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿الْعَقَبَةَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle and ما is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿أَدْراكَ﴾: a past verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of ما, and the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿مَا الْعَقَبَةُ﴾: mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the nominal clause stands in place of the second object of أدراك.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿فَكُّ﴾: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿رَقَبَةٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is explicative.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿أَوْ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿إِطْعامٌ﴾: conjoined to فك; ﴿فِي يَوْمٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them; ﴿ذِي﴾: naʿt (adjective) of يوم; ﴿مَسْغَبَةٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿يَتِيماً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of إطعام; ﴿ذا مَقْرَبَةٍ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of يتيما, muḍāf to مقربة.

daas-irab:16-16.t: Conjoined to the preceding verse, and its i'rab is clear.

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿كانَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of kāna; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿وَتَواصَوْا﴾: conjoined to آمنوا; ﴿بِالصَّبْرِ﴾: attached to the verb; ﴿وَتَواصَوْا بِالْمَرْحَمَةِ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); ﴿الْمَيْمَنَةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and the relative noun is mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿بِآياتِنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿هُمْ أَصْحابُ﴾: mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is the khabar of الذين; ﴿الْمَشْأَمَةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause الذين… is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:20-20.t: ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, the fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿نارٌ﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿مُؤْصَدَةٌ﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is resumptive.

dervis-irab:1-20.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْبَلَدِ) In al-Qāmūs: "(البلد) and (البلدة) is Mecca, may Allah the Exalted honour it, and every tract of land that is enclosed, whether inhabited or desolate, and the soil; (البلد) is also the grave, the cemetery, the house, the trace, and the ostrich's nest-hollow" and so on, until he says: "(بلد بالمكان بلودا) means he stayed and kept to it, or took it as a town."
(حِلٌّ) One says (حلّ) and (حلال), and (حرم) and (حرام), in one meaning. (حلّ في المكان) means he alighted in it; (يحل), with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, (حلولا), so he is (حال) and the place is (محلول فيه). More of its meaning will come in the section on I'rab.
(كَبَدٍ) Toil and hardship; he endures the calamities of this world and the hardships of the next. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "(الكبد), with two fatḥas, is hardship, from (المكابدة) of a thing, which is bearing the hardships of doing it." The wording of al-Zamakhsharī is: "Its origin is from (كبد الرجل) (كبد), of the pattern ṭariba, so he is (أكبد), when his liver pains him and swells; then it was extended until it was used for every weariness and hardship, and from it (المكابدة) was derived, just as it was said (كبته الله) in the sense of 'He destroyed him', whose origin is (كبده), i.e. He struck his liver. Labīd said, lamenting his brother Arbad:
يا عين هلّا بكيت اربد إذ ... قمنا وقام الخصوم في كبد
(O eye, why did you not weep for Arbad when we rose, and the adversaries rose in distress?)
that is, in the severity of the affair and the difficulty of the matter." Now among the strange features of the letters kāf and bāʾ is that when they occur as the first and second radicals of a word they indicate hardness, hardship and subjugation. One says (كببته في الهوّة) "I threw him into the pit", and (كبكبته), and (كببته), and likewise when someone is thrown from the top of a mountain or a wall; the horseman (يكبّ) the wild beasts, and they (يكبون العشار). He said:
يكبّون العشار لمن أتاهم ... إذا لم تسكت المائة الوليدا
(They slaughter the pregnant she-camels for whoever comes to them, when the hundred does not quiet the newborn.)
Among the figurative uses: (أكبّ على عمله), and he is (مكب عليه), meaning devoted to it, never leaving it. Labīd said: "The bending of the Hālikī over his hands, bent over (مكبّا), examining the notches of the arrowheads." (كبت الله عدوّك) means Allah subdued your enemy and destroyed him; and you say: "May your adversary never cease to be (مكبوتا) and your enemy (مكبوتا)." (كبح فرسه) means he pulled its rein until its head stood erect; for this reason it was also said: "(في كبد) means upright, not made to walk on all fours taking things with his mouth, nor on his belly, because Allah, Blessed and Exalted, honoured the children of Adam with things of which this is one." Another Bedouin said: "What is it with the falcon, that it loves the hare as it does not love the (خرب)?" He said: "Because it (يكبح) its moustache and turns it back", that is, it strikes its moustache with its droppings and soils it. (كبر الأمر) and (خطب كبير), and (كبر علي ذلك) means it was hard on you: (كبر على المشركين ما تدعوهم إليه). (كبر الرجل في قدر) and (كبر في سنّه), and (شيخ كبير) and (ذو كبر وكبر); and the condition of (الكبرة) and (المكبرة) is advanced age and the hardship and effort it entails. He said:
عجوز عليها كبرة في ملاحة ... أقاتلتي يا للرجال عجوز
(An old woman, on whom is age along with charm; will she kill me, O men, an old woman?)
(كبس الحفرة) means he filled it in; (كبس رأسه في جيب قميصه) means he put it into it; and he is (عابس كابس); and the nightmare (الكابوس) fell upon him. (انتطحت الكباش) the rams butted each other; (كبش كتيبة) is the leader of a battalion, and they are (كباش الكتائب). He said:
وإنّا لمما نضرب الكبش ضربة ... على رأسه تلقي اللسان من الفم
(We are of those who strike the ram a blow on its head that throws the tongue out of the mouth.)
(فلان مكلّب مكبل) means a man bound with (الكلب), which is rawhide strap, shackled with (الكبل), which is the fetter; (كبلت الأسير) and (كبّلته) and (اكتبلته); and on his shanks are (كبل) and (كبول). Jarīr said:
ومكتبلا في القدّ ليس بنازع ... له من مراس القدّ رجلا ولا يدا
(Shackled in the strap, not freeing from the grip of the strap either a foot or a hand of his.)
And (كبا لوجهه) "he fell on his face". You say: "the sharp edge turns back and fortune stumbles", and so on to the end of this wonderful material in our beloved language.
(لُبَداً) Abundant, heaped one upon another, and its depletion is not feared because of its quantity; (وما له سبد ولا لبد) is also said, and this is what is meant here. (لبد) was also the last of the vultures of Luqmān. It is said that he sent ʿĀd to the Sanctuary to pray for rain for them; when they were destroyed, Luqmān was given the choice between the survival of seven droppings of dun gazelles on a rugged mountain that no rain touches, or the survival of seven vultures, each time one vulture died another succeeding it. He chose the vultures, and the last of them was Lubad; when it died, Luqmān died. That was in the time of al-Ḥārith al-Rāʾish, one of the kings of Yemen. The poets mentioned him; al-Nābigha said:
أضحت خلاء وأضحى أهلها احتملوا ... أخنى عليها الذي أخنى على لبد
(She became empty and her people departed; what destroyed Lubad destroyed her.)
(النَّجْدَيْنِ) The two ways, meaning the way of good and the way of evil. (النجد) is a road on a height. It was also said that they are the two breasts; this is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿAlī, because they are like the two ways for the life of the child and his sustenance. (النجد) is height, its plural (نجود); from it Najd was named, for its elevation above the low-lying Tihāma. In al-Qāmūs: "(النجد) is what rises above the land, its plural (أنجد), (أنجاد), (نجاد), (نجود), and (نجد), and the plural of (النجود) is (أنجدة); it is the clear raised road and whatever is the opposite of (الغور), that is Tihāma; its jīm is also given ḍamma; masculine; its upper part is Tihāma and Yemen, its lower part Iraq and Syria, and its beginning from the side of the Hijaz is Dhāt ʿIrq. It is also what a house is furnished with, of rugs, bedding and cushions, the plural being (نجود) and (نجاد); the skilled guide; and a place with no trees" until he says "and the breast."
(الْعَقَبَةَ) The hard road in a mountain. (اقتحامها) is passing through it. More on this discussion will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(مَسْغَبَةٍ) A mīm-prefixed verbal noun from (سغب يسغب سغبا), of the pattern fariḥa: he was hungry. In al-Qāmūs: "(سغب), like (فرح) and (نصر), (سغبا) and (سغبا) and (سغابة) and (سغوبة) and (مسغبة) means he was hungry, so he is (ساغب), (سغبان) and (سغب), and she is (سغبى), plural (سغاب). (السغب) is also thirst, but it is not in use."
(مَتْرَبَةٍ) In al-Mukhtār: "(ترب الشيء) means dust touched it, of the pattern ṭariba; from it (ترب الرجل) means he became poor, as if he clung to the dust. (تربت يداه) is a curse upon him, meaning may he gain no good. (تربه تتريبا فتترّب) means he smeared it with dust and it became smeared; (أتربه) means he put dust on it. In the ḥadīth: 'Put dust on the writing, for it is more apt to succeed in the need.' (أترب الرجل) means he became rich, as if he came to have wealth as much as the dust. (المتربة) is destitution and poverty, and (مسكين ذو متربة) means one who clings to the dust." Ibn Khālawayh said:
"Abū ʿAbd Allāh Niftawayh informed us from Thaʿlab, who said: One says (ترب الرجل) when he became poor and (أترب) when he became rich, and its meaning is that his wealth became like dust in quantity. If someone asks:
'If the matter is as you claim, then what is the point of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ saying to the man who consulted him about marriage: "Take the one with religion, (تربت يداك)", when the Prophet does not curse any of the believers?' there are answers to that, and two of them are preferred. The first is that he, peace be upon him, intended a supplication that is not meant to take effect, like their saying to a man when praising him: 'May Allah fight him, how poetic he is', and 'May Allah disgrace him, how learned he is'. The poet said, speaking of a woman he loved, and he is Jamīl Buthayna:
رمى الله في عيني بثينة بالقذى ... وفي الغر من أنيابها بالقوادح
وفي وجهها الصافي المليح بقتمة ... وفي قلبها القاسي بودّ مماتح
(May Allah cast a mote in the eyes of Buthayna and decay in her bright teeth, and a dimness in her clear, fair face, and in her hard heart a love that draws out [his life].)
The second answer is that this speech came from the Messenger ﷺ in the manner of a condition, as if he had said: 'Take the one with religion, (تربت يداك) if you do not do what I have commanded you.' This is fine, and it is the choice of Thaʿlab and al-Mubarrad."
(مُؤْصَدَةٌ) Closed over, with hamza, which is the reading of Ḥafṣ, Abū ʿAmr and Ḥamza; and with a silent wāw, which is the reading of the rest. They are two dialects. One says (أصدت الباب), (آصدته) and (أوصدته) when you shut it and closed it. It was also said that the meaning of the hamzated form is "closed over" and the meaning of the non-hamzated is "locked"; al-Qāmūs did not distinguish between them.

* I'rab:
(لا أُقْسِمُ بِهذَا الْبَلَدِ وَأَنْتَ حِلٌّ بِهذَا الْبَلَدِ)
The i'rab of (لا أقسم) and the view that (لا) is redundant have often preceded, so renew your acquaintance with it. (بهذا) is attached to (أقسم), and (البلد) is a badal for (هذا). The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or parenthetical. (أنت) is mubtadaʾ, (حلّ) is the khabar, (بهذا) is attached to (حل), and (البلد) is a badal. al-Zamakhsharī preferred that the wāw be parenthetical and the clause an interjected one, and Abū Ḥayyān rejected him. What follows is the wording of al-Zamakhsharī and Abū Ḥayyān's rejection.
al-Zamakhsharī said: "He, Glory be to Him, swore by the Sacred Land and what follows on the point that man was created immersed in the toil of hardships and trials, and interjected between the oath and what is sworn upon His saying: (وأنت حلّ بهذا البلد), meaning: among the hardships is that one like you, despite the greatness of your sanctity, is treated as lawful in this Sacred Land, as game is treated as lawful outside the Sanctuary" until he says: "Or he consoled the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by swearing by his city, to the effect that man is never free from enduring hardships, and he interjected by promising him the conquest of Mecca, to complete the consolation and relief for him, so He said: (وأنت حل بهذا البلد), meaning: you will be free in it in the future, doing in it what you wish of killing and capture" until he says: "If you say: where is a parallel to His saying (وأنت حلّ) in the sense of the future? I say: His saying, Mighty and Majestic, (إنك ميت وإنهم ميّتون); and the like of it is wide-spread in the speech of people: you say to one whom you promise honour and gifts: 'You are honoured, given gifts', and it is wider still in the speech of the Arabs, because future states are, in their view, like those present and witnessed. And sufficient as a decisive proof that it is for the future, and that interpreting it as present is impossible, is that the sūra is by agreement Meccan, so how far is the Hijra from the time of its revelation, let alone the conquest?"
Abū Ḥayyān said: "Taking the clause as parenthetical is not necessary. We mentioned at the outset that it is a circumstantial clause and showed the fineness of its place, which is to convey the magnification of that by which the oath is sworn; and it is a concurrent ḥāl, neither anticipated nor narrated, so it is not an announcement of the future. As for his question and answer, this is not something that would be asked by anyone with the slightest connection to the science of grammar, because announcement may be about future things, and the active participle and what takes its course, when predicated or used as an attribute, need not be taken as present, but may be for the past at times, for the present at others and for the future at others; and this is among the first principles of grammar. As for his saying 'sufficient as a decisive proof…' etc., it is nothing, because we did not take (وأنت حل) to mean that it becomes lawful to you what you do in Mecca of capture and killing at the time of its revelation in Mecca, such that they would conflict; rather we took it to mean that he resides there in particular, and at the time of revelation he was necessarily residing there. Also, what he relates of agreement that it was revealed in Mecca is not correct, and disagreement over it is sometimes reported from some people."
We have cited this debate only because the strength of argument on both sides moved all the commentators, roughly speaking, to maintain modesty in this dispute; therefore we too did not wish to give a preference. However, al-Karkhī supported al-Zamakhsharī's view, saying: "Allah swore by the Sacred Land that He created man in hardship, and interjected between them by promising him the conquest of Mecca, to complete the consolation, in His saying (وأنت حلّ), i.e. in it in the future, doing what you wish of killing and capture." Likewise al-Jalāl in his commentary supported al-Zamakhsharī, saying: "The clause is an interjection between the oath and what is sworn upon." al-Samīn followed him, citing his words and saying: "It was also said that it is circumstantial and (لا) is negative, i.e. 'I do not swear by this land while you are residing in it, because of the greatness of your worth', that is, 'I do not swear by anything, while you are more entitled to be sworn by than it.'" Ibn Khālawayh supported Abū Ḥayyān.
(وَوالِدٍ وَما وَلَدَ)
Conjoined to the preceding oath. What is meant by (الوالد) is Adam; (ما) is conjoined to (والد), and the clause (ولد) is the ṣila, i.e. his offspring. Better than that is what Abū Ḥayyān said: "The apparent sense is that His saying (ووالد وما ولد) does not intend a particular one but applies to every father." As for al-Zamakhsharī, he leaned towards another opinion, saying: "If you ask: what is meant by (والد وما ولد)? I say: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his offspring. He swore by his city, which is his birthplace, the sanctuary of his father Ibrāhīm and the place where his [other] father Ismāʿīl grew up, peace be upon them both, and by the one who begot them and by him. If you ask: why was it indefinite? I say: for the vagueness that stands alone in praise and wonder. If you ask: why was it not said (ومن ولد)? I say: in it is what is in His saying: (والله أعلم بما وضعت), meaning something placed, wondrous in its matter." al-Farrāʾ said: (ما) is for people, like His saying (ما طاب لكم), and (وما خلق الذكر والأنثى), while He is the Creator of the male and the female.
(لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ فِي كَبَدٍ)
The clause is the answer to the oath; the lām occurs in the answer; (قد) is a particle of certainty; (خلقنا) is a verb and an agent; (الإنسان) is a direct object, and the (أل) in it is generic, since He meant the genus of man; (في كبد), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to an omitted ḥāl from (الإنسان), i.e. enduring hardships, standing upright on his two feet, performing his role in building his society, not like the animal that takes its food with its mouth.
(أَيَحْسَبُ أَنْ لَنْ يَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ أَحَدٌ)
The hamza is for denial and rebuke. (يحسب) is an imperfect nominative verb whose agent is latent, returning to man, or to some of the chiefs of Quraysh from whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ endured what he endured. (أن) is the lightened form of (أنّ), and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); (لن) is a particle of negation, accusative and future; (يقدر) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by (لن); (عليه), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to (يقدر); and (أحد) is the agent of (يقدر).
It is strange that Ibn Khālawayh says what is literally: "(أن) is an accusative particle, (لن) is an accusative particle, and (يقدر) is accusative by (لن); and when the Arabs combine two operating particles, they cancel one of them." This is nonsense beyond which there is no nonsense, a flagrant breach of the consensus of the grammarians, who cite this very verse. For it is a condition that when the opened (أنّ) is lightened, its noun is a pronoun of the matter, and its mention has been heard only in poetic necessity, as in the saying of Janūb, sister of ʿAmr Dhū al-Kalb:
وقد علم الضيف والمرملون ... إذا اغبرّ أفق وهبت شمالا
بأنك ربيع وغيث مريع ... وأنك هناك تكون الثمالا
(The guest and the destitute know, when the horizon turns dusty and the north wind blows, that you are spring and fertile rain, and that you, there, are the refuge.)
Here its noun came as a mentioned pronoun, not of the matter. As for its khabar, it must be a clause; then if the clause is nominal, or verbal with a verb that is inert or one of supplication, no separator is needed. The nominal: (وآخر دعواهم أن الحمد لله رب العالمين). The verbal whose verb is inert: (وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى). The verbal whose verb is supplication: (والخامسة أن غضب الله عليها). In other cases a separator is obligatory, to be a compensation for what they dropped from (أنّه), namely one of the two nūns and the noun, or so that it is not confused with the maṣdar (أن). The separation is by (قد), because it brings the past close to the present, as in (ونعلم أن قد صدقتنا); or by a particle of futurity, as in (علم أن سيكون); or by a negative with (لا), (لن) or (لم). An example with (لن) is (أيحسب أن لن يقدر عليه أحد). If it is said: "They have made it obligatory that it be the lightened one after a verb of knowing, but after a verb of thinking they have permitted it to be either lightened or maṣdar", I say: how lofty is the style of the Qur'an above thrusting in two operators of one meaning and our being forced to cancel one of them; this is something above which the style of the Great Qur'an stands.
(يَقُولُ أَهْلَكْتُ مالًا لُبَداً)
The clause is circumstantial or resumptive. The saying is by way of boasting and pride. The clause (أهلكت) is the content of the saying; (مالا) is a direct object; and (لبدا) is an adjective.
(أَيَحْسَبُ أَنْ لَمْ يَرَهُ أَحَدٌ)
The question is for denial and rebuke as well, and its i'rab is like that of the preceding one.
(أَلَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهُ عَيْنَيْنِ وَلِساناً وَشَفَتَيْنِ وَهَدَيْناهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ)
The hamza is for an affirmative question; (لم) is a particle of negation, inversion and the jussive; (نجعل) is an imperfect verb jussive by (لم); (له), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to (نجعل), because it is in the sense of (نخلق); (عينين) is a direct object; (ولسانا وشفتين) are conjoined to (عينين). (الشفة) has an omitted lām; the original is (شفهة), by the evidence of its diminutive (شفيهة) and its plural (شفاه); its parallel is (سنة). It is not pluralised with alif and tāʾ, being independent of that by its broken plural (شفاه). (هديناه) is a past verb, an agent and a direct object; (النجدين) is a second direct object, or accusative by removal of the preposition, as preceded.
(فَلَا اقْتَحَمَ الْعَقَبَةَ وَما أَدْراكَ مَا الْعَقَبَةُ)
The fāʾ is a conjunction and (لا) is negative; this is the view of Abū ʿUbayda, al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj, as if He had said: "We granted him the limbs and guided him to the path, yet he did no good, i.e. he did not (اقتحم)." al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj said: (لا) was mentioned only once, whereas the Arabs hardly use (لا) alone with the past verb without repeating it, as in His saying (فلا صدق ولا صلّى); He used it alone only because the end of the speech indicates its meaning, so it is possible that His coming saying (ثم كان…) etc. stands in place of the repetition, as if He had said "he did not enter the steep path and did not believe". It was also said that it follows the course of supplication, as in His saying (لا نجا ولا سلم), a supplication against him that he do no good. al-Zamakhsharī, after faulting the statement of al-Farrāʾ, al-Zajjāj and Abū ʿUbayda, said: "It is in the sense of (لا) repeated in meaning, because the meaning of (فلا اقتحم العقبة) is 'he neither freed a neck nor fed a poor man'; do you not see that He explained the entering of the steep path in this way?" This works for him only on the reading of one who read (فكّ) as a past verb. Yet the strangest thing we have read is the statement of Shaykh al-Jalāl that (لا) is in the sense of (هلّا), i.e. a particle of urging; al-Jalāl relied on a report from Abū Zayd, but we have never heard that (لا) alone is for urging without the hamza with it. The wording of Ibn Hishām in al-Mughnī: "As for the saying of the Exalted, Glory be to Him: (فلا اقتحم العقبة), (لا) in it is repeated in meaning, because the meaning is 'he neither freed a neck nor fed a poor man', for that is the explanation of the steep path; so said al-Zamakhsharī. al-Zajjāj said: it is permissible only because (ثم كان من الذين آمنوا) is conjoined to it and enters into the negation, as if it were said: 'he neither entered nor believed'. If this were sound, it would be permissible to say (لا أكل زيد وشرب). Some said (لا) is supplicatory, a supplication against him that he do no good. Another said: it is urging, the original being (فألّا اقتحم), then the hamza was dropped; and this is weak." From reviewing these opinions it becomes clear that taking it as supplicatory is the more preferable and more fitting to the style of the Noble Qur'an. al-Damāmīnī said: "This is a view of evident fineness with no dust upon it, so it would have been better to put it before the other opinions." (اقتحم العقبة): a past verb, a latent agent, its implied form being "he", i.e. the speaker, and a direct object. More on the meaning of entering the steep path will come in the section on Rhetoric. The wāw is parenthetical. (ما) is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the clause (أدراك) is the khabar of (ما). (ما) is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ, and (العقبة) its khabar; the nominal clause, suspended by the interrogative, is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the second object of (أدراك). The clause is parenthetical, thrust in to make the steep path plain and to confirm the sense of vagueness and explanation: for His saying (وما أدراك ما العقبة) is the very same steep path, because a word defined by alif-lām, when repeated, the second is the same as the first.
(فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ أَوْ إِطْعامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ يَتِيماً ذا مَقْرَبَةٍ أَوْ مِسْكِيناً ذا مَتْرَبَةٍ)
(فكّ رقبة) is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is the freeing", the implied form being "what is the entering of the steep path? It is the freeing of a neck, or feeding…" etc. This implied muḍāf was needed only so that the explained and the explanation correspond. Do you not see that the explanation (المفسِّر), with kasra on the sīn, is a verbal noun, while the explained (المفسَّر), with fatḥa on the sīn, which is the steep path, is not a verbal noun? Had the muḍāf not been implied, the verbal noun (فكّ) would be explaining the entity (العقبة). It was also read (فكّ رقبة) with (فكّ) as a past verb whose agent is "he" and (رقبة) its object; the verbal clause is then a badal for His saying (اقتحم العقبة) negated by (لا), as if it were said: "he neither freed a neck nor fed", and this supports the view of al-Zamakhsharī. (أو إطعام) is conjoined to (فكّ رقبة) on the first reading; (في يوم), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to (إطعام); (ذي مسغبة) is an adjective of (يوم); (يتيما) is the object of (إطعام) as a verbal noun that has met the conditions for governing the accusative, or the object of (أطعم) on the other reading; (ذا مقربة) is an adjective of (يتيما); (أو) is a conjunction; (مسكينا) is conjoined to (يتيما); and (ذا متربة) is an adjective of (مسكينا).
(ثُمَّ كانَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَتَواصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ وَتَواصَوْا بِالْمَرْحَمَةِ)
(ثم) is a conjunction conveying distance in rank, because faith is the foundation and the first, and no deed is complete without it. (كان) is a defective past verb, its noun is latent, returning to him; (من الذين) is its khabar; the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila; (وتواصوا) is conjoined to the ṣila and falls within its scope; (بالصبر), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to (تواصوا); and (وتواصوا بالمرحمة) is also conjoined.
(أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآياتِنا هُمْ أَصْحابُ الْمَشْأَمَةِ عَلَيْهِمْ نارٌ مُؤْصَدَةٌ)
(أولئك) is mubtadaʾ and (أصحاب الميمنة) is the khabar. (الذين) is mubtadaʾ, the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila, and (بآياتنا), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to (كفروا). (هم) is mubtadaʾ and (أصحاب المشأمة) is its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of (الذين). A valuable discussion of the difference in forms of expression will come in the section on Rhetoric. (عليهم) is a fronted khabar, (نار) is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and (مؤصدة) is an adjective of (نار); the clause is a second khabar, and you may make it resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying (وهديناه النجدين) there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya): He borrowed (النجدين) for good and evil, omitted the thing likened, which is good and evil, and retained the thing to which it is likened. If you say: the likening of good to the height, which is the raised part of the road, is beyond dispute because it is apparent, unlike evil, which is a descent and a falling from the peak of the natural disposition to the depths of vulgarity, we say: He joined them either by way of preponderance, or on the imagination's fancy that in it are ascent, falling back and descent; and this is among the most eloquent and most marvellous of speech.
2- In His saying (فلا اقتحم العقبة) there is a ranking embellishment (tarshīḥ) of the metaphor, by mentioning what suits the thing likened to. Examples of it have passed, and we add here that the basis of tarshīḥ is to pretend to forget the likening, and its sayings are claim and exaggeration. For this reason tarshīḥ is more eloquent than tajrīd, which is mentioning what suits the thing likened, without the thing likened to, because in it is an admission of the likening, such that what is built on spatial height is built on loftiness of rank likened to spatial height, as Abū Tammām said:
ويصعد حتى يظن الجهول ... بأن له حاجة في السماء
(He ascends until the ignorant think he has a need in the sky.)
He borrowed ascent for loftiness of rank, then built upon it what is built on height of place. Were it not that his aim was to forget the likening and insist on denying it, making him ascend in the sky, this speech would have no point. Furthermore, they do this forgetting even with an explicit statement of the likening and admission of the origin; so with denial of the origin and insistence on it, as in the metaphor, it is all the more fitting, as in the saying of al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Aḥnaf:
هي الشمس مسكنها في السماء ... فعزّ الفؤاد عزاء طويلا
فلن تستطيع إليها الطلوع ... ولن تستطيع إليك النزولا
(She is the sun, whose dwelling is in the sky; so console the heart with a long consolation. You will never be able to rise to her, and she will never be able to descend to you.)
It is not hidden that this forgetting occurred along with admission of the origin, namely (هي) in his saying (هي الشمس), because it returns to the beloved, and this is plain; and making it the pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa), as some imagined, is a strain.
Among the examples of the bare metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-mujarrada) is also the saying of the poet:
فإن يهلك فكل عمود قوم ... من الدنيا إلى هلك يصير
(If he perishes, then every pillar of a people from this world goes to perdition.)
In his saying (عمود) there is an original explicit metaphor: he likened the chief of the people to a pillar, on the ground that both bear a load; the indicator is (يهلك); and in (إلى هلك يصير) there is tajrīd. Tarshīḥ and tajrīd may also be combined, since it is permissible to forget the likening in some attributes and not in others. An example is the saying of Abū al-Ṭayyib:
سقاك وحيّانا بك الله إنما ... على العيس نور والخدور كمائمه
(May Allah give you drink and greet us through you; for upon the camels is a blossom, and the howdahs are its calyxes.)
(النور) is the flower, or the white of it, and what is meant by it here is women, the common ground being beauty; the metaphor is an original explicit one; in the mention of the howdahs there is tajrīd and in the mention of the calyxes there is tarshīḥ; and such a metaphor is then called absolute (muṭlaqa).
3- In His saying (أولئك أصحاب الميمنة والذين كفروا هم أصحاب المشأمة) the expression was varied. He pointed to the believers as an honour to them and to show that they are present with Him, the Exalted, in the station of His generosity, as if sitting before Him, the matter amounting to no more than pointing at them with the finger; then He used the word of pointing that indicates distance, and did not say (هؤلاء), announcing the remoteness of their rank with Him and their attaining the honour of favour and nearness to Him. As for the disbelievers, He mentioned them with the pronoun of the absent third person, pointing to the fact that they are absent from the station of His manifestations and the splendours of His outpourings, and that they do not deserve to have a relation to Him even through the feeblest of ties. This is among the greatest of wonders, so ponder it.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنتَ حِلٌّ بِهَـٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدِ﴾.
He says: it is lawful for you; He made it lawful on the day of the conquest of Mecca. It was not lawful before it and will not be lawful after it.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَوَالِدٍ وَمَا وَلَدَ﴾.
He swore by Adam and his offspring. (ما) is acceptable for people; similar to it is: ﴿وَمَا خَلَقَ الذَّكَرَ وَالأُنْثَى﴾ — and He is the creator of the male and the female — and similar to it: ﴿فَانكِحُوا مَا طابَ لَكُم مِن النِّسَاءِ﴾, and He did not say: من طاب.
Likewise: ﴿ولا تَنْكِحُوا مَا نَكَحَ آباؤُكُمْ مِن النِّساءِ﴾. All of this is permissible in Arabic. (ما) together with what follows it may also be in the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun), as in His saying: ﴿والسَّماءِ وَمَا بَنَاهَا﴾, ﴿وَنَفْسٍ وَمَا سَوَّاهَا﴾, as though He said: by the sky and its building, and a soul and its fashioning; and a father and his begetting; and His creating the male and the female. Whichever way you take it, it is correct.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلإِنسَانَ فِي كَبَدٍ﴾.
He says: upright and erect. It is also said: created in toil (كبد) — he was created to labour and struggle with the affair of this world and the affair of the Hereafter. [138/a] It was revealed about a man of Banū Jumaḥ who was given the kunya Abū al-Ashaddayn. He used to put the ʿUkāẓ leather under his feet, then order ten men to pull it from under his feet, and the leather would tear while his feet did not move. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿أَيَحْسَبُ﴾ (5) — because of his strength — ﴿أَن لَّن يَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ أَحَدٌ﴾ (5), while Allah has power over him. Then He said: he says: "I have spent much wealth in enmity to Muhammad ﷺ", and he is lying. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿أَيَحْسَبُ أَن لَّمْ يَرَهُ أَحَدٌ﴾ (7) in his spending.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَقُولُ أَهْلَكْتُ مَالاً لُّبَداً﴾.
اللبد: much. Some said its singular is لُبدة and لُبَد is a plural. Some took it as a singular on the pattern of قُثَم and حُطَم; in both interpretations it means much. Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī read: "مالاً لُبَّداً", with shadda, like رُكَّع; as though he meant: مالٌ لابدٌ, and مالان لابدان, and أموالٌ لُبَّد. الأموال and المال may have one meaning.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَهَدَيْنَاهُ ٱلنَّجْدَينِ﴾.
The two highways (النجدان): the way of good and the way of evil.
He said: [Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: [al-Kisāʾī narrated to me, saying: Qays narrated to me] and Qays narrated to me from Ziyād ibn ʿIlāqa from Abū ʿUmāra from ʿAlī, may Allah have mercy on him, concerning His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَهَدَيْنَاهُ ٱلنَّجْدَينِ﴾. He said: good and evil.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلاَ ٱقتَحَمَ ٱلْعَقَبَةَ﴾.
No other clause containing (لا) was joined to His saying [فلا اقتحم], although the Arabs hardly ever use (لا) singly in speech without repeating it in another clause, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَلاَ صَدَّقَ وَلاَ صَلَّى﴾ and ﴿لا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾. [That is] because it is one of those whose meaning is at its end, so one sufficed for another. Do you not see that He explained the scaling of the steep pass by two things, saying: ﴿فَكّ رَقبةً، أو أطعم فى يومٍ ذى مسغبة﴾, then ﴿ثم كان [من الذين آمنوا]﴾, so He explained it by three things? So it is as though at the beginning of the speech it was: he did neither this, nor this, nor this.
The general public read: ﴿فَكُّ رَقَبةٍ (13) أو إِطعامٌ﴾ (14), and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read: "فَكَّ رقبةً", and so did ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib. [Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us], saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: And Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl al-Marwazī narrated to me from ʿAṭāʾ from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān from ʿAlī that he read it: "فَكَّ رقبةً أو أطعمَ". That is the closer of the two to correct Arabic, because الإطعام is a noun, and a noun should be coordinated with a noun like it; so if it were said: ثم إن كان أشكلُ للإطعام والفك [Translator's note: the sentence is garbled in the source; the sense is: «ثم كان» (a verb) matches the verbal forms better than the nouns الإطعام and الفك]. So we chose: فكَّ رقبةً, because of His saying: "ثم كان". The other interpretation is permissible: you imply (أن) in it and drop it [138/b], so it becomes [«فكيون» in the source, read «فيكون»] like the poet's saying:
ألا أيهاذا الزَّاجِرى أحْضُرَ الْوغى * وأَنْ أَشْهَدَ اللَّذَّاتِ هل أنتَ مُخْلِدِى
(O you who chide me for attending battle and for partaking in pleasures — can you make me live forever?)
Do you not [«ألاى» in the source] see that the appearance of (أن) at the end of the speech indicates that it is coordinated with another like it at the beginning of the speech, which he dropped?

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ﴾.
[A day] of famine. If it were "ذا مسغبة", you would make it an attribute of the orphan, as though He said: or feeding, on a day, an orphan who is in hunger, or a poor man. [Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us], saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: And Ḥibbān narrated to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās that he passed by a poor man clinging to the dust out of need, and said: This is the one of whom Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿أَوْ مِسْكِيناً ذا مَتْرَبَةٍ﴾ (16). ﴿والموصَدة﴾ (20): it is read with hamza and without hamza, and it means: closed over.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «لا»: negating; the oath is negated to magnify the thing sworn by; «البلد» is a badal (substitute).

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «ووالد»: a noun conjoined to the first «هذا البلد», and «ما»: a relative noun conjoined to «والد».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: (لقد خلقنا الإنسان في كبد) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The lām occurs in the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam); the preposition «في كبد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الإنسان».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: «أن»: lightened (mukhaffafa), and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the clause «لن يقدر» is the khabar (predicate) of «أن»; and «أن» with what follows it is to be interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) standing in place of the two objects of حسب.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: (أيحسب أن لم يره أحد) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] Its i'rab was given in verse (5).

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The preposition «له» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نجعل», which means "We create".

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: «النجدين» is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: (فلا اقتحم العقبة) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The clause is resumptive, and the clause «ما العقبة» is the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: «فك»: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: «هي فك» (it is the freeing).

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: «يتيمًا»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of {إِطْعَامٌ}; «ذا»: naʿt (adjective) of «يتيمًا».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The clause «ثم كان» is conjoined to the clause «لا اقتحم».

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: (أولئك أصحاب الميمنة) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «عليهم نار» is a second khabar (predicate) of للذين كفروا.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (لا أقسم بهذا البلد): (لا) is redundant (zāʾida). It is also said that it means (ألا) [Translator's note: printed «الا»; possibly the opening particle «ألا» is meant]. It is also said that (لا) is not redundant and is a rejection of speech before it. (البلد) is a naʿt (adjective) of (هذا), or a badal (substitute), or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition).

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying (أن لن يقدر): (أن) [with its clause] stands in place of the two objects of (حسب). Its like is (أن لم يره أحد). The origin of (يره) is (يرآه); then the hamza was lightened, and the alif was dropped for the jussive.

mekki-muskil:12-13.t: His saying (وما أدراك ما العقبة فك رقبة): (فك) is a badal (substitute) from (العقبة), or with an implied (هي): "it is the freeing", a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The discussion of the parallel of (وما أدراك) has already preceded in al-Ḥāqqa and elsewhere.

mekki-muskil:15-15.t: His saying (يتيما): accusative governed by (إطعام), and (أو مسكينا) is conjoined to it.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿لا﴾: negating, or connective (ṣila).
﴿أقسم﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿بهذا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أقسم﴾.
﴿البلد﴾: a corresponding badal (substitute) for ﴿هذا﴾, nominative. [Translator's note: so in the source («مرفوع»); as a badal of the genitive ﴿هذا﴾ it would be genitive, as the source itself says under the next ayah.]

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿وأنت﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or parenthetical, and «أنت» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿حل﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative.
﴿بهذا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿حل﴾.
﴿البلد﴾: a corresponding badal (substitute) for ﴿هذا﴾, genitive (majrūr); the clause is parenthetical, with no grammatical position, or circumstantial, the implied sense being: "No, I swear by this city while you are a dweller (حالٌّ), i.e. residing, in this city"; and it was said: the meaning is "No, I swear by it while you are made lawful (مُستحَلّ) in it", i.e. harming you is made lawful.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿ووالد﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «والد» is conjoined to the preceding oath, genitive (majrūr).
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun conjoined to ﴿والد﴾, genitive.
﴿ولد﴾: a past verb, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); the clause ﴿ولَدَ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿لقد﴾: the lām is in the answer of the oath, and «قد» is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq).
﴿خلقنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent).
﴿الإنسان﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿في كبد﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿الإنسان﴾; the clause ﴿خلقنا﴾ is the answer of an oath, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿أيحسب﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (inkārī), and «يحسب» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو).
﴿أن﴾: lightened from the heavy form (anna), and its noun (ism) is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn).
﴿لن﴾: a particle of negation.
﴿يقدر﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb); the clause ﴿لن يقدر...﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of ﴿أن﴾.
﴿عليه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يقدر﴾.
﴿أحد﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative; «أن» and what falls within its scope are in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of ﴿يحسب﴾, and the clause ﴿يحسب...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿يقول﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو).
﴿أهلكت﴾: a past verb, and the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿أهلكت﴾ is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿مالا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿لبدا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿مالا﴾, accusative (manṣūb); the clause is circumstantial, in the position of accusative, or resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿أيحسب﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (inkārī), and «يحسب» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو).
﴿أن﴾: lightened from the heavy form (anna), and its noun (ism) is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn).
﴿لم﴾: a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive.
﴿يره﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿لم يره...﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «أن».
﴿أحد﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative; «أن» and what falls within its scope are in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of ﴿يحسب﴾, and the clause ﴿يحسب...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿ألم﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīrī), and «لم» is a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive.
﴿نجعل﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾.
﴿له﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نجعل﴾.
﴿عينين﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ, because it is a dual.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿وهديناه﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿النجدين﴾: second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), or accusative by removal of the preposition.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿فلا﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and «لا» is negating or for supplication (duʿāʾiyya).
﴿اقتحم﴾: a past verb, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو).
﴿العقبة﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أدراك﴾: a past verb, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو), and the kāf is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿أدراك﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of «ما».
﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ.
﴿العقبة﴾: khabar, nominative (marfūʿ); the clause ﴿ما العقبة﴾ is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the second and third objects of the verb ﴿أدراك﴾, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative. The clause ﴿وما أدراك...﴾ is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿العقبة﴾ in the previous ayah.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿فك﴾: khabar (predicate) of a concealed mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is the freeing of a neck" (هي فك رقبة).
﴿رقبة﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). The nominal clause is resumptive by way of explanation (bayāniyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿أو﴾: a conjunction.
﴿إطعام﴾: conjoined to ﴿فك رقبة﴾, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿في﴾: a preposition.
﴿يوم﴾: a noun in the genitive (majrūr); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿إطعام﴾.
﴿ذي﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿يوم﴾.
﴿مسغبة﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿يتيمًا﴾: object of ﴿إطعام﴾.
﴿ذا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿يتيمًا﴾, accusative (manṣūb) by the alif.
﴿مقربة﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the kasra.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿أو﴾: a conjunction.
﴿مسكينًا﴾: conjoined to ﴿يتيمًا﴾, accusative (manṣūb).
﴿ذا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿مسكينًا﴾, accusative by the alif.
﴿متربة﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction conveying a delay in rank.
﴿كان﴾: a deficient past verb, and its noun (ism) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو).
﴿من﴾: a preposition.
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa in the position of genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) its omitted khabar (predicate).
﴿آمنوا﴾: a past verb, and the pronoun is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
﴿وتواصوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «تواصوا» is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿تواصوا﴾ is conjoined to ﴿آمنوا﴾, falling within the scope of the ṣila.
﴿بالصبر﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تواصوا﴾.
﴿وتواصوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «تواصوا» is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿تواصوا﴾ is likewise conjoined to ﴿آمنوا﴾, falling within the scope of the ṣila.
﴿بالمرحمة﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تواصوا﴾; the clause ﴿كان من الذين﴾ is conjoined to ﴿فلا اقتحم﴾.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿أولئك﴾: a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أصحاب﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿الميمنة﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra; the clause has no grammatical position, because it is resumptive.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿والذين﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; «الذين» is mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿كفروا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
﴿بآياتنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كفروا﴾.
﴿هم﴾: in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ.
﴿أصحاب﴾: khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ.
﴿المشأمة﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); the nominal clause is the khabar of ﴿الذين﴾.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿عليهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿نار﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿مؤصدة﴾: an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿نار﴾; the clause is a second khabar of ﴿الذين﴾, or resumptive, with no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
Concerning لا there are three views. Al-Akhfash said: it is a connective (ṣila, i.e., redundant) — this is one view. It has been said: it is in the sense of ألا (the opening particle "indeed"); al-Akhfash also mentioned this. The third view is the view of the exegetes (ahl al-taʾwīl): al-Ḥasan narrated from Mujāhid, who said: «لا» is a rejection of their speech; then He began: أُقْسِمُ بِهذَا الْبَلَدِ.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic, الْبَلَدِ there are three views: it is a naʿt (adjective) of هذا; it is a badal (substitute); and the most fitting is the third, that it is a ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). The grammarians mention ʿaṭf bayān in general terms, and I know of no one who explained it and the difference between it and the badal except Ibn Kaysān. He said: the difference between them is that the meaning of the badal is that you put the second in the place of the first, as though you had not mentioned the first; and the meaning of ʿaṭf bayān is that you assume that, if you mentioned the first noun alone, it would not be known except by the second, and if you mentioned the second alone, it would not be known except by the first, so you brought it to clarify the first, standing for it in the place of the naʿt and the tawkīd (emphasis). He said: the demonstration of this is in the vocative: يا أخانا زيد أقبل ("O our brother, Zayd, come forward") is on the badal, as though you had removed the first and said: يا زيد. If you intend ʿaṭf bayān, you say: يا أخانا زيدا أقبل.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: (النجدين is) a second object from which إلى was omitted, on the view of the Basrans. Likewise Sībawayh recited: [al-Kāmil] 565- كما عسل الطّريق الثّعلب ("as the fox trotted along the road"): according to him, the preposition was dropped from it; according to the Kufans, it is an adverb (ẓarf) like amām and quddām (in front).

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
It is said: the way of «لا» in the like of this is that it comes repeated, as in فَلا صَدَّقَ وَلا صَلَّى [al-Qiyāma: 31]; and Sībawayh permitted it singly, and recited: [Majzūʾ al-Kāmil] 566-
من صدّ عن نيرانها ... فأنا ابن قيس لا براح
(Whoever turns away from its fires — I am Ibn Qays: no retreat!)
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd (al-Mubarrad) disagreed with him and made this a poetic necessity (iḍṭirār). As for the verse, it has the meaning of repetition, because He, Mighty and Majestic, explained the meaning of the steep path (al-ʿaqaba) with something that is repeated. Qatāda said: the Fire is a steep path before the Garden.

nahhas-irab:12-13.t:
The implied form is: the scaling of the steep path is to free a neck (i.e., a slave), as Abū Hurayra narrated from the Prophet ﷺ: «Whoever frees a slave, Allah, Glorified, frees for every limb of it a limb of his from the Fire». Abū Hurayra said: even his private part for its private part.
Al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr and al-Kisāʾī read فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ أَوْ إِطْعامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ [Translator's note: the vowelling printed is the standard one; the reading of these readers is فَكَّ رَقَبَةً أَوْ أَطْعَمَ, with past verbs, as the discussion below shows]. Then the grammarians discussed this. Al-Farrāʾ chose this reading and argued that after it comes ثم كان, i.e., since كان, a past verb, is conjoined to the first, it must be «فكّ» so that a past verb is conjoined to a past verb. Al-Akhfash, Abū Ḥātim and Abū ʿUbayd chose the other reading.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Religion forbids attacking the reading by which the community read, and it cannot have been taken except from the Prophet ﷺ; and he, peace be upon him, said: «The Qur'an was revealed in seven aḥruf». So they are two good readings, and neither may be put ahead of the other. As for al-Farrāʾ's objection based on كان and on conjunction with the first, it is not binding, because it is not permissible that it be conjoined according to the meaning [Translator's note: so in the text; the sense may be "because it may be conjoined according to the meaning"], since the meaning is "he did this". And he himself contradicted his statement by permitting the other reading on the implication of «أن», and he recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 567-
ألا أيّهذا اللّائمي أحضر الوغى ... وأن أشهد اللّذّات هل أنت مخلدي
(O you who blame me for attending the battle and for witnessing pleasures — will you make me immortal?)
He means أن أحضر; and if the matter were as he said, he would have put أحضر in the accusative. And implying «أن» is not permissible except with a compensation, because it is part of a noun.
Abū ʿUbayd objected, saying: the choice is «فكّ رقبة», because it explains the steep path. And it is reported that Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna said: everything about which He, Mighty and Majestic, said وما أدراك, He has explained, and whatever He said وما يدريك about, He has not explained. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a mistake: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said وَما أَدْراكَ مَا الْقارِعَةُ [al-Qāriʿa: 3] and, exalted be His mention, said ما أَدْراكَ مَا الْحَاقَّةُ [al-Ḥāqqa: 3], and after this there is no explanation.
It is narrated from al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ that they read «وأطعم في يوم ذا مسغبة». Al-Farrāʾ said — although he did not mention who read «ذا مسغبة» — it is an adjective of يتيم, i.e., an orphan possessing hunger. Abū Jaʿfar said: The error in this is very clear, because an adjective may not precede the thing described, and I do not know how this occurred to him such that he mentioned it in the book «al-Maʿānī»! Rather, «ذا مسغبة» is in the accusative by أطعم, and يتيما is a badal (substitute) for it.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: ثُمَّ كانَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا, i.e., he remained firm in faith; and it has been said: ثم is for (sequence in) informing. وَتَواصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ وَتَواصَوْا بِالْمَرْحَمَةِ: the verb and the bāʾ were repeated for emphasis (tawkīd).

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: I.e., they are taken toward the right, to the Garden, and the people of the Fire toward the left, to the Fire.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: Al-Akhfash said: ḥill and ḥalāl (lawful), and ḥirm and ḥarām (sacred/forbidden) [Translator's note: i.e., حِلٌّ in وَأَنْتَ حِلٌّ بِهذَا الْبَلَدِ is equivalent to حلال].

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: Whoever takes it from aṣada should pronounce it with hamza, and whoever takes it from awṣada may not pronounce it with hamza.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
وَوالِدٍ: the wāw is a conjunction (wāw ʿaṭf), not a wāw of oath, and likewise وَما وَلَدَ. Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī said:
وَوالِدٍ is Ibrāhīm ﷺ, and his child (is what he begot). It has been narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: the father is the one who begets, and وَما وَلَدَ is his child.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is on the basis that it is general, and it seems the clearest thing that is said; and the implied form may be "by a father and his begetting", so that «ما» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned it. Among the clearest things said about its meaning is the saying of ʿAṭāʾ, who said: فِي كَبَدٍ means in struggling with affairs. Al-Ḥasan said: he struggles with prosperity and adversity, and no one struggles with affairs as the son of Adam struggles. Saʿīd ibn Abī al-Ḥasan said: he struggles with the affair of this world and the affair of the Hereafter. Mujāhid said: he is a drop of fluid and a clinging clot, and he does not cease to be in struggle. These views go back to one meaning, and it is the clearest thing that has been said about it, i.e., he struggles with affairs and labours at them. This is the apparent meaning of kabad in the speech of the Arabs. Dhū al-Iṣbaʿ al-ʿAdwānī said: [al-Basīṭ] 563-
لي ابن عمّ لو أنّ النّاس في كبد ... لظلّ محتجرا بالنّبل يرميني
(I have a cousin who, were people in hardship, would stay girded with arrows shooting at me.)
And Labīd said: [al-Munsariḥ] 564- قمنا وقام الخصوم في كبدي
(We stood, and the adversaries stood in hardship.)

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: It has been said that by this is meant the disbeliever, i.e., does he think that Allah will not have power over him and punish him? So He, exalted be His praise, informed of his ignorance.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: It has been said: he wards off with this (saying) the doing of good deeds; and it has been said: he said this out of regret, and what comes after it indicates this answer. Abū Jaʿfar said: لبد may be the plural of lubda, and it may be a singular like ḥuṭam. It is narrated from Abū Jaʿfar (al-Qāriʾ) that he read لبّدا, the plural of lābid [Translator's note: the text reads «لا بد»], and from Mujāhid that he read لبدا (lubudan), the plural of labūd. We know of no disagreement about its meaning: that it is "much".

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: The original is يرأه; the vowel of the hamza was shifted onto the rāʾ, so it took fatḥa, and the hamza fell away. Abū Jaʿfar said: I know of no one among the grammarians who discussed the reason why the hamza falls away (rather than remaining) when its vowel is cast onto what precedes it, except ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān; I asked him about it, and he said: when the vowel of the hamza dropped and it became quiescent, and the rāʾ before it was quiescent, it was given an accidental vowel, so its status was that of a quiescent letter, and after it was a quiescent letter, so what came after it — the hamza — was deleted.

nahhas-irab:8-9.t: (The word) lisān (tongue) is treated as masculine and feminine: whoever makes it masculine forms its plural as alsina, and whoever makes it feminine says alsun. He said: and in its diminutive, lusayyin with doubled yāʾ and lusayna with it undoubled. The original of shafa (lip) is shafha, and the evidence for that is its plural, its diminutive and the derivation of the verb from it.

safi-cedvel:1-4.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) is redundant (zāʾida) «[Note: it is said to be negative, with the (الواو) after it circumstantial and the clause a ḥāl, i.e.: "I do not swear by this city while you reside in it, because of your high standing — or while it is made lawful in it — rather I swear by you"]». (بهذا) is attached to (أقسم). (الواو) is parenthetical. (بهذا) is attached to (حلّ). (والد) is conjoined to the first (هذا), genitive. (ما) is a relative noun in the position of genitive, conjoined to (والد). (اللام) is the lām of the oath. (قد) is a particle of confirmation. (في كبد) is attached to a ḥāl from the object.
Clause: «لا أقسم ... » has no grammatical position (inceptive).
And the clause: «أنت حلّ ... » has no grammatical position (parenthetical).
And the clause: «ولد ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما)).
And the clause: «خلقنا ... » has no grammatical position (answer to the oath).

* Morphology:
(4) كبد: a noun meaning hardship, or a maṣdar of the triliteral كبد الرجل when his liver pains him (the pattern of فرح), then used for every kind of weariness; its wazn is فعل (with two fatḥas).

safi-cedvel:5-5.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for threatening interrogation. (أن) is the lightened form of the heavy (أنّ), and its noun is an omitted pronoun referring to الإنسان, i.e. "that he". (عليه) is attached to (يقدر); the interpreted maṣdar (أن لن يقدر..) is in the position of accusative, standing in for the two objects of يحسب.
Clause: «يحسب ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).
And the clause: «لن يقدر عليه أحد ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the lightened (أن).

safi-cedvel:6-6.t:
* I'rab:
The agent pronoun in (يقول) refers to a specific person «[Note: he is Abū l-Ashadd ibn Kalada — with ḍamma on the shīn — or Usayd ibn Kalada]».
Clause: «يقول ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).
And the clause: «أهلكت ... » is in the position of accusative as the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl).

* Morphology:
(لبدا) plural of لبدة, a noun meaning abundance; the wazn of لبدة is فعلة (with ḍamma and sukūn), and the plural is فعل (with ḍamma then fatḥa) «[Note: and see verse (19) of Sūrat al-Jinn.]».

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
The i'rab of its counterpart has preceded «[Note: in verse (5) of this sūra]», in words and clauses, and the interrogation here is one of denial.

safi-cedvel:8-17.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for reproachful interrogation. (له) is attached to an omitted second direct object «[Note: or attached to (نجعل), made to include the meaning "We create"]». (الواو) is a conjunction in the three places.
Clause: «نجعل ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).
And the clause: «هديناه ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the resumptive clause).
Verses 10–11: (الفاء) is a conjunction. (لا) is a negative particle «[Note: the verses came without repeating (لا), because the end of the speech indicates its repetition, i.e. "so he neither undertook the steep path nor believed ..."; according to Abū Zayd it means هلّا, as an urging particle]». (الواو) is parenthetical. (ما) is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) in both places; the khabar of the first is the clause أدراك, and the khabar of the second is (العقبة), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the undertaking of the steep path".
And the clause: «لا اقتحم العقبة ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause هديناه).
And the clause: «ما أدراك ... » has no grammatical position (parenthetical).
And the clause: «أدراك ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ما).
And the clause: «ما العقبة ... » is in the position of accusative as the second direct object of (أدراك).
Verses 11–17: (فكّ) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "it is" (هي). (أو) is a conjunction in both places. (إطعام) is conjoined to فكّ, nominative «[Note: it may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the clause being conjoined to the clause (هي) فكّ by the conjunction أو]». (في يوم) is attached to the maṣdar إطعام. (يتيما) is a direct object of the maṣdar إطعام. (مسكينا) is conjoined to (يتيما), accusative. (ثمّ) is a conjunction. (من الذين) is attached to the khabar of كان. (بالصبر) is attached to the first (تواصوا). (بالرحمة) is attached to the second (تواصوا).
And the clause: « (هي) فكّ ... » has no grammatical position (explanatory resumptive).
And the clause: «كان من الذين ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause لا اقتحم) «[Note: it falls under the sense of negation, or it is affirmative if there is no negation in the first clause]».
And the clause: «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين)).
And the clause: «تواصوا ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause آمنوا).
And the clause: «تواصوا (الثانية) » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause تواصوا (the first)).

* Morphology:
(9) شفتين: dual of شفة, a noun denoting the known organ of the face. In شفة the lām is omitted: the original is شفهة, by the evidence of its diminutive شفيهة and its plural شفاه. It is not pluralised in the sound plural, so the wazn of شفة is فعة (with two fatḥas).
(10) النجدين: dual of نجد, a noun meaning the elevated road, here meant as the road of good and the road of evil; it is also said that they are the two breasts. The wazn of نجد is فعل (with fatḥa and sukūn).
(11) العقبة: a noun for a difficult path in a mountain; it is borrowed here for striving against the self in doing acts of obedience and abandoning forbidden things, or it is an embellishment (tarshīḥ) for the metaphor of النجدين for good and evil. Its wazn is فعلة (with three fatḥas).
(13) فكّ: a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral فكّ (the pattern of نصر); its wazn is فعل (with fatḥa and sukūn).
(14) مسغبة: a maymī maṣdar of the triliteral سغب (the pattern of فرح), with the tāʾ added for intensity, or of the pattern of نصر; its wazn is مفعلة (with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn).
(15) مقربة: like مسغبة, from the pattern of كرم.
(16) متربة: like مسغبة, from the pattern of فرح, i.e. dust touched him, meaning he became poor.
(17) المرحمة: like مسغبة, from the pattern of فرح.

* Rhetoric:
1- Istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya (explicit metaphor): in His words, the Exalted «وَهَدَيْناهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ».
That is, the two paths of good and evil: He borrowed النجدين for good and evil, omitting the likened and retaining the thing likened to; and He described the path of good as lofty and elevated, unlike the path of evil, in which there is a descent from the peak of the natural disposition to the depth of wretchedness; so this is by predominance (taghlīb), or by the imagination's fancy.
2- Istiʿāra (metaphor): in His words, the Exalted «فَلَا اقْتَحَمَ الْعَقَبَةَ».
العقبة is the rugged road in a mountain, and in the sea it is what is difficult in it and an ascent. Here it is a metaphor for what it has been explained by: the arduous deeds of lofty rank with Allah, the Exalted; the contextual indicator is evident, and the affirmation of "undertaking", by which the act and effort are meant, is an embellishment (tarshīḥ).

* Benefits:
- The maṣdar's acting like its verb:
In these two verses the maṣdar acts like its verb, in His words, the Exalted (أَوْ إِطْعامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ. يَتِيماً ذا مَقْرَبَةٍ): the maṣdar إطعام acted like its verb and governed an object, namely (يتيما).
We shall explain below what relates to the maṣdar's acting like its verb.
The explicit maṣdar acts like its verb in two cases:
1- If it is valid to put (أن and the verb) in its place, as in the noble verse, by the interpretation (أو أن تطعم يتيما), or (ما and the verb), as in His words, the Exalted (تَخافُونَهُمْ كَخِيفَتِكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ), the estimate being: (كما تخافون أنفسكم). The maṣdar acts in this state whether it is annexed, as in His words, the Exalted: (وَلَوْلا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النَّاسَ بَعْضَهُمْ بِبَعْضٍ لَفَسَدَتِ الْأَرْضُ), or has tanwīn, as in the noble verse, or has (آل), which is very rare in the language, as in the poet's verse:
ضعيف النكاية أعداءه ... يخال الفرار يراخي الأجل
(Weak in harming his enemies; he thinks flight prolongs one's term.)
The point of citation in it is the maṣdar (النكاية), which put أعداءه in the accusative as an object.
2- If it stands in for the verb: such as (أداء الواجب) (حفظا الحقّ): these are two maṣdars that stand in for their verbs. The estimate is "perform the duty", "guard the right". The maṣdar in this case is parsed as an absolute object of an omitted verb. This maṣdar standing in for the verb is always accusative and keeps one state wherever it occurs.

safi-cedvel:18-20.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is a conjunction. (بآياتنا) is attached to (كفروا). (هم) is a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is (أصحاب). (عليهم) is attached to a fronted khabar of the postponed mubtadaʾ (نار).
Clause: «أولئك أصحاب ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).
And the clause: «الذين كفروا ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the resumptive clause).
And the clause: «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين)).
And the clause: «هم أصحاب ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
And the clause: «عليهم نار ... » is in the position of nominative as a second khabar «[Note: or it is an explanatory resumptive clause with no grammatical position]».

* Morphology:
(20) مؤصدة: a passive participle from the quadriliteral آصد meaning "closed over"; its wazn is مفعلة (with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn).

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {ثُمَّ كَانَ}: [«ثُمَّ» here is] for the delay (tarākhī) of faith and its distance in rank and merit from freeing the slave and giving charity, not in time, because faith is what comes first and no deed is established except through it; al-Zamakhsharī said this. It was also said: the meaning is: then he was, at the outcome of his affair, among those who met death in a state of faith, because meeting death upon it is a condition for benefiting from acts of obedience. It was also said: the delay is in the mention [only], and its explanation has already been given.

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {مُّؤْصَدَةُ}: Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ read it with a hamza, and the rest with a wāw; likewise in [Sūrat] «al-Humaza». The first reading is from آصَدْتُ البابَ, i.e. "I closed the door", أُوْصِدُه, so it is مُؤْصَدٌ. It was said: it may also be from أَوْصَدْتُ, but he gave a hamza to the quiescent wāw because of the ḍamma before it, just as he gave a hamza in {بالسوق والأعناق} [Ṣād: 33], as has preceded. The second reading likewise admits both roots, the hamza having been lightened because it is quiescent after a ḍamma. Al-Farrāʾ transmitted from al-Sūsī — whose rule is to replace such a hamza — that he does not replace this one after a ḍamma, and they explained that by [the danger of] confusion. And it happens that «مُوْصَدة» with a wāw was read by one whose rule is to pronounce the hamza fully. What is apparent is that the two readings are from two roots: the first from آصَدَ يُؤْصِد like أَكْرَم يُكْرِم, and the second from أَوْصَدَ يُوصِدُ, like أَوْصَلَ يُوْصِلُ. The poet said:
4576 - تَحِنُّ إلى أجْبِالِ مكةَ ناقتي ... ومِنْ دونِها أبوابُ صنعاءَ مُوْصَدَهْ
(My she-camel yearns for the mountains of Mecca, while before her stand the gates of Ṣanʿāʾ, shut.)
i.e. closed. Another said:
4577 - قوماً يُعالِجُ قُمَّلاً أبناؤُهمْ ... وسلاسِلاً حِلَقاً وباباً مُؤْصَدا
(A people whose sons struggle with lice, with ringed chains and a shut door.)
Abū Bakr, the transmitter from ʿĀṣim, disliked the hamza in this word, and he — may Allah have mercy on him — said: «We have an imam who reads "مؤصدة" with a hamza, and I would like to block my ears when I hear him.» I say: it seems he preserved from his shaykh only the omission of the hamza, although Ḥafṣ preserved it [the hamza] from him, and Ḥafṣ was more precise in [ʿĀṣim's] reading than Abū Bakr according to what the Qurʾān readers have transmitted, even though Abū Bakr was older, more meticulous and more trustworthy in the view of the people of ḥadīth.
And His saying: {عَلَيْهِمْ نَارٌ} may be a resumptive (mustaʾnafa) clause, or a second khabar (predicate), or the khabar may be «عليهم» alone with «نار» as its fāʿil (agent), and this is the best.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {وَأَنتَ حِلٌّ بهذا البلد}: there are two views on it. First: the clause is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya), in one of two senses. Either in the sense that He, exalted is He, swore by this city and what follows it that man was created in toil (kabad), and this clause was interposed between the two — meaning: part of the toil is that one like you, despite the greatness of your inviolability, is treated as lawful game in this city, just as game is treated as lawful outside the sanctuary. Or in the sense that He swore by His city that man is never free from enduring hardships, and interposed a promise to him of the conquest of Mecca, to complete the consolation; so He said: "and you will be free (ḥill) in it" in what lies ahead, doing in it what you wish of killing and taking captive — so «حِلٌّ» means ḥalāl (permitted). Al-Zamakhsharī said the substance of that. Then he said: "If you say: where is a parallel to his saying «وأنت حِلٌّ» in the sense of the future? I say: the saying of the Exalted {إِنَّكَ مَيِّتٌ وَإِنَّهُمْ مَّيِّتُونَ} [al-Zumar: 30].
