The like of it is widespread in the speech of [Allah's] servants: you say to someone to whom you promise honour and gifts, 'you are honoured and gifted'; and in the speech of Allah the Exalted it is more widespread, because future states are, in His sight, like present, witnessed ones. Sufficient as decisive proof that it is for the future, and that interpreting it as the present is impossible, is that the sūra is by agreement Meccan — and how far the Hijra is from the time of its revelation, let alone the conquest!" The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] disputed with him in a way that does not hold, and rejected his claim of consensus on its revelation in Mecca on the basis of a disagreement reported by Ibn ʿAṭiyya.
The second of the two first views: the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. I do not swear by this city while you are dwelling in it, because of the greatness of your standing — i.e. He does not swear by a thing while you are more worthy of being sworn by than it. It has also been said: the meaning is: I do not swear by it while you are treated as lawful in it, i.e. harming you is treated as lawful. The discussion of the like of this «لا» preceding the verb of the oath was given before.

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {وَمَا وَلَدَ}: it has been said: «ما» means «مَنْ» (who); it has also been said: it is maṣdariyya — He swore by the person and by his act. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was it not said «ومَنْ وَلَدَ»? I say: there is in it what there is in his saying {والله أَعْلَمُ بِمَا وَضَعَتْ} [Āl ʿImrān: 36], i.e. [Allah knows best] what thing she delivered, i.e. something delivered of wondrous significance." It has also been said: «ما» is negative, so it needs an implied relative noun by which the speech becomes sound, its implied form being: "and the one who did not beget"; since what is meant by the father is the one to whom a child is born, and by the one who did not beget, the barren. The substance of this was said by Ibn ʿAbbās and his students Ibn Jubayr and ʿIkrima.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا}: this is what is sworn to. Al-kabad is hardship. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its origin is from kabida al-rajulu kabadan, so he is akbad, when his liver (kabid) aches and swells; then its use was extended until it was used for every exertion and hardship. From it al-mukābada (enduring) was derived, just as it was said kabatahu in the sense of 'he destroyed him', its original being kabadahu, i.e. he struck his liver." Labīd said:
4573 - يا عَيْنُ هَلاَّ بَكَيْتِ أَرْبَدَ إذ ... قُمْنا وقام الخُصومُ في كَبَدِ
(O eye, why did you not weep for Arbad when we stood up and the adversaries stood up in hardship?)
[Translator's note: this verse number is as printed; the same number was printed earlier, at al-Burūj 14.]
i.e. in the severity of the matter and the difficulty of the affair. And Dhū al-Iṣbaʿ said:
4574 - ليَ ابنُ عَمّ لَوَانَّ الناسَ في كَبَدٍ ... لظلَّ مُحْتَجِراً بالنَّبْلِ يَرْمِيْني
(I have a cousin who, were people in hardship, would keep himself fenced in with arrows, shooting at me.)

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {يَقُولُ أَهْلَكْتُ}: [the clause] may be resumptive or a ḥāl (circumstantial). The majority read «لُبَداً» with ḍamma on the lām and fatḥa on the bāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar doubled the bāʾ, and from him also its sukūn is reported. Mujāhid and Ibn Abī al-Zinād read it with two ḍammas. The discussion of this word and the disagreement on it was given in al-Jinn.

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying: {وَشَفَتَيْنِ}: al-shafa (lip) has its final radical omitted; the original is shafaha, as shown by its diminutive shufayha and its plural shifāh; a parallel is sana (year) in one of the two dialectal forms. Shāfahtuhu means: I spoke to him without intermediary. It is not pluralised with alif and tāʾ, its broken plural sufficing in place of the sound plural.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {النجدين}: either an adverb (ẓarf), or on the omission of the preposition, if what is meant by them is the two breasts. Al-najd is originally "the neck, because of its height". It has also been said: the high road, as in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
4575 - فريقانِ منهمْ قاطعٌ بَطْنَ نَخْلَةٍ ... وآخرُ منهمْ جازعٌ نَجْدَ كَبْكَبِ
(Two parties: one of them crossing the hollow of Nakhla, and the other traversing the high road of Kabkab.)
From it comes «نَجْدٌ» [the region of Najd], because of its height above Tihāma.

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {فَلاَ اقتحم}: al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj said: "He mentioned «لا» only once, and the Arabs hardly ever use «لا» singly with a past verb without repeating it, as in the saying of the Exalted {فَلاَ صَدَّقَ وَلاَ صلى} [al-Qiyāma: 31]. He used it singly only because the end of the speech indicates its meaning; so his saying {ثُمَّ كَانَ مِنَ الذين آمَنُواْ} [al-Balad: 17] may stand in place of the repetition, as if He said: he neither attempted the steep ascent nor believed." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is repeated in meaning, because the meaning of 'he did not attempt the steep ascent' is: he did not free a slave and did not feed a poor person — do you not see that He explained attempting the steep ascent by that?" The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This only works for him on the reading of «فَكَّ» as a past verb."

semin-durr:13-13.t:
Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr and al-Kisāʾī read «فَكَّ» as a past verb, «رقبةً» in the accusative, and «أو أَطْعم» also as a past verb. The rest read «فَكُّ» with ḍamma on the kāf, as a noun, «رقبةٍ» genitive by annexation, and «أو إطعامٌ» likewise a nominative noun. In the first reading, the verb is a badal (substitute) from his saying «اقتحمَ», so it is an explanation of it, as if it were said: he did not free a slave and did not feed. In the second, «فَكُّ» is nominative on an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. it is the freeing of a slave or feeding, in the sense of permitting [either]. In the speech there is an omitted muḍāf, indicated by «فلا اقتحمَ», its implied form being: "and what will make you know what attempting the steep ascent is?"; so the implied form is: attempting the steep ascent is the freeing of a slave or feeding. This muḍāf had to be implied only so that the explanation and the thing explained correspond: do you not see that the explanation (al-mufassir, with kasra on the sīn) is a maṣdar (verbal noun), while the thing explained (al-mufassar, with fatḥa on the sīn), namely the steep ascent, is not a maṣdar? So had we not implied a muḍāf, the maṣdar, namely «فَكُّ», would be explaining a concrete thing, namely the steep ascent.
The Commander of the Faithful [ʿAlī] and Abū Rajāʾ read «فَكَّ أو أطعمَ» as two verbs, as mentioned, except that they read «ذا» in the accusative, with alif. Al-Ḥasan read «إطعامٌ» and «ذا», likewise with alif. On these two readings it is the object of «أَطْعم» or «إطعامٌ», and «يتيماً» is then a badal from it or a naʿt (adjective) of it. In the reading of the majority it is «ذي», with yāʾ, as a naʿt of «يوم», figuratively: the day is described as hungry, for intensiveness, as in their saying "your night is standing [in prayer] and your day is fasting". The agent of «إطعام» is omitted; this is one of the places in which omitting the agent alone is regular according to the Basrans, and I have set them out in full, praise be to Allah.
Al-masghaba is hunger with weariness, and it is sometimes said of thirst with weariness; al-Rāghib said this. One says from it: saghiba al-rajulu yasghabu saghban and sughūban, so he is sāghib and saghbān; and al-masghaba is the pattern mafʿala from it. Likewise al-matraba from al-turāb (dust). One says: tariba, i.e. he became poor until his skin stuck to the dust. As for atraba with alif, it means "he became rich", like athrā, i.e. his wealth became like dust and like earth. And al-maqraba is likewise the pattern mafʿala from al-qarāba (kinship). Al-Zamakhsharī has a sweet expression here; he said: "Al-masghaba, al-maqraba and al-matraba are mafʿalas from saghiba, when he was hungry; qaruba, in lineage; and tariba, when he became poor."

ukberi-tibyan:1-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَا أُقْسِمُ بِهَذَا الْبَلَدِ (١) وَأَنْتَ حِلٌّ بِهَذَا الْبَلَدِ (٢) وَوَالِدٍ وَمَا وَلَدَ (٣) لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ فِي كَبَدٍ (٤)).
The words of the Exalted (لَا أُقْسِمُ بِهَذَا الْبَلَدِ) are like (لَا أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ). It is also said [the meaning is]: I do not swear by it while you are made lawful (ḥill) in it; rather, I swear by you. (وَوَالِدٍ) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «الْبَلَدِ», and «مَا» is in the sense of «مَنْ» (who); and the answer of the oath is «لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا».
(فِي كَبَدٍ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. «مُكَابِدًا» (enduring hardship).

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَا اقْتَحَمَ الْعَقَبَةَ (١١)).
The words of the Exalted (فَلَا اقْتَحَمَ): «لَا» is in the sense of «مَا» (not); and most often something like this comes repeated, as in (فَلَا صَدَّقَ وَلَا صَلَّى).

ukberi-tibyan:12-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْعَقَبَةُ (١٢) فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ (١٣) أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ (١٤) يَتِيمًا ذَا مَقْرَبَةٍ (١٥)).
The words of the Exalted (مَا الْعَقَبَةُ), i.e. «مَا اقْتِحَامُ الْعَقَبَةِ» (what is the scaling of the steep path); because He explained it with the words of the Exalted «فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ», which is an act, whether it comes in the form of the verb or in the form of the maṣdar (verbal noun). «الْعَقَبَةُ» is a concrete thing, so it is not explained by an act. So whoever reads «فَكَّ» or «أَطْعَمَ» explained the maṣdar with the verbal clause, because it indicates it.
And whoever reads «فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ», the implied form is «هُوَ فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ» (it is the freeing of a slave); the maṣdar is annexed to its object, and «إِطْعَامٌ» is not annexed; and there is no pronoun in either of them, because the maṣdar does not carry a pronoun.
Some of the Basrans held that when the maṣdar governs the object, there is a pronoun in it like the pronoun in the active participle. (يَتِيمًا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (إِطْعَامٌ).

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ كَانَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا. . . (١٧)).
The words of the Exalted (ثُمَّ): here it is for the sequence of the reports, not for the sequence of what is reported.

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (عَلَيْهِمْ نَارٌ مُؤْصَدَةٌ (٢٠)).
Whoever pronounces «مُؤْصَدَةٌ» with hamza took it from «آصَدَ الْبَابَ» (he closed the door); and whoever does not pronounce the hamza, it may be that he lightened the hamza, or that it is from «أَوْصَدَهُ». And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Balad
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لا أُقْسِمُ بِهَذا البَلَدِ﴾: by "the town" here Mecca is meant. The meaning is: ”أُقْسِمُ بِهَذا البَلَدِ“ ("I swear by this town"), and ”لا“ was inserted for emphasis (tawkīd), just as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لِئَلا يَعْلَمَ أهْلُ الكِتابِ﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 29] ("so that the People of the Book may know"). It was also read: ”لَأُقْسِمُ بِهَذا البَلَدِ“, in which case the lām is the lām of the oath and of emphasis. This reading is rare, and it is far-fetched in Arabic, because the lām of the oath does not enter a future-tense verb unless the nūn [of emphasis] is with it: you say ”لَأضْرِبَنَّ زَيْدًا“ ("I will surely strike Zayd"), and ”لَأضْرِبُ“ is not permitted when you mean the present. And Sībawayh and al-Khalīl claimed that this lām enters together with ”إنَّ“, and so it is made sufficient in the chapter of ”إنَّ“: you say ”إنِّي لَأُحِبُّكَ“ ("I surely love you").

zajjaj:2-2.t: And the meaning of ﴿وَأنْتَ حِلٌّ بِهَذا البَلَدِ﴾ ("and you are free [of restriction] in this town"): Mecca was made lawful for the Prophet, peace be upon him, for an hour of the day, and it was not lawful for anyone before him nor for anyone after him. And the meaning of ”أُحِلَّتْ لَهُ“ ("it was made lawful for him") is: its game was made lawful for him, and that its fresh herbage be cut and its trees be lopped. One says: ”رَجُلٌ حِلٌّ“, ”حَلالٌ“ and ”مُحَلٌّ“ (a man in the non-sacral state); and likewise ”رَجُلٌ حَرامٌ“, ”حِرْمٌ“ and ”مُحْرِمٌ“ (a man in the sacral state).

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿وَوالِدٍ وما ولَدَ﴾ ("and by a begetter and what he begot"): it has come in the exegesis that its meaning is Adam and his offspring; and its meaning has also come as: every begetter and every one begotten.

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ خَلَقْنا الإنْسانَ في كَبَدٍ﴾: this is the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam). The meaning is: "I swear by these things: We have certainly created the human being in kabad", that is, he endures hardship (yukābidu) in his affairs in this world and the Hereafter. And it was said: ﴿فِي كَبَدٍ﴾ means he was created upright, walking on his two legs, while all other things and animals are not upright. And it was said ﴿فِي كَبَدٍ﴾: the human being was created in his mother's womb with his head toward her head, and when she wishes to give birth the head turns downward.

zajjaj:5-5.t: And His saying: ﴿أنْ لَنْ يَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ أحَدٌ﴾ ("that no one has power over him"): this, it has come in the exegesis, is a man who was extremely strong. An ʿUkāẓī hide used to be spread out for him, and he would stand on it and it would be torn apart, so that nothing came out from under his feet except in pieces, because of his strength. He was called Kalada. So it was said: "Does he think, because of his strength, that no one has power over him, and that he will not be resurrected?!" And it was said: "[Does he think] that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has no power over him?" — because he did not believe in the Resurrection.

zajjaj:6-6.t: ﴿يَقُولُ أهْلَكْتُ مالا لُبَدًا﴾ ("he says: I have squandered heaps of wealth"). It was read: ”أهْلَكْتُ مالًا لُبَدًا“, and it is also read: ”لُبَّدًا“. The meaning of ”لُبَدًا“ is "much", part of it matted (lubbida) onto part. The pattern ”فُعَلٌ“ is for abundance: one says ”رَجُلٌ حُطَمٌ“ when a man smashes (ḥaṭm) a great deal. And whoever reads ”لُبَّدًا“, it is the plural of ”لابِدٌ“.

zajjaj:7-7.t: ﴿أيَحْسَبُ أنْ لَمْ يَرَهُ أحَدٌ﴾ ("does he think that no one saw him?"): that is, does he think that what he spent is not counted against him? And in the discourse there is evidence that he claimed he had spent a great deal which did not benefit him.

zajjaj:8-9.t: And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ألَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهُ عَيْنَيْنِ﴾ ﴿وَلِسانًا وشَفَتَيْنِ﴾ ﴿وَهَدَيْناهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ﴾ [al-Balad: 10] ("Have We not made for him two eyes, and a tongue and two lips, and guided him to the two highways?"): that is, have We not done for him that by which one infers that Allah is able to resurrect him and to count against him what he does?!

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿وَهَدَيْناهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ﴾: the two clear ways. ”اَلنَّجْدُ“ is raised ground. So the meaning is: "Have We not made known to him the way of good and the way of evil, as clear as the clarity of two elevated roads?!"

zajjaj:11-11.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَلا اقْتَحَمَ العَقَبَةَ﴾: the meaning is ”فَلَمْ يَقْتَحِمِ العَقَبَةَ“ ("but he did not attempt the steep ascent").
Just as He said: ﴿فَلا صَدَّقَ ولا صَلّى﴾ [al-Qiyāma: 31] ("for he neither affirmed nor prayed"). Here He mentioned ”لا“ only once, whereas the Arabs rarely speak in such a position without ”لا“ twice or more; you would hardly say ”لا حَيَّيْتَنِي“ meaning ”ما حَيَّيْتَنِي“ ("you did not greet me"), but if you said "[لا] حَيَّيْتَنِي ولا زُرْتَنِي" ("you neither greeted me nor visited me") it would be sound. [Translator's note: the source reads «حَيَّيْتَنِي ولا زُرْتَنِي» without the first «لا»; the argument requires «لا حَيَّيْتَنِي ولا زُرْتَنِي».] The meaning [of the repeated lā] in ﴿فَلا اقْتَحَمَ العَقَبَةَ﴾ is present: a second ”لا“ is as if it were in the discourse, because His saying ﴿ثُمَّ كانَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ [al-Balad: 17] ("then he was of those who believed") points to the meaning ”فَلا اقْتَحَمَ العَقَبَةَ ولا آمَنَ“ ("he neither attempted the steep ascent nor believed").

zajjaj:13-14.t: It was read: ﴿فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ﴾ ﴿أوْ إطْعامٌ في يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ﴾ ("the freeing of a slave, or feeding on a day of hunger"), and it was read: ”فَكَّ رَقَبَةً أوْ أطْعَمَ في يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ“ ("he freed a slave or fed on a day of hunger"), and both are permissible. Whoever said ﴿فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ﴾, the meaning is: "attempting the steep ascent is the freeing of a slave or feeding"; and whoever read ”فَكَّ رَقَبَةً“, it is construed according to the sense. And ”اَلْمَسْغَبَةُ“ is famine.

zajjaj:15-15.t:
And His saying: ﴿يَتِيمًا ذا مَقْرَبَةٍ﴾: its meaning is "possessed of kinship". You say: ”زَيْدٌ ذُو قَرابَتِي، وذُو مَقْرَبَتِي“ ("Zayd is one of my kin"), whereas ”زَيْدٌ قَرابَتِي“ is ugly, because ”اَلْقَرابَةُ“ is the maṣdar (verbal noun). The poet said:
يَبْكِي عَلَيْهِ غَرِيبٌ لَيْسَ يَعْرِفُهُ ∗∗∗ وذُو قَرابَتِهِ في الحَيِّ مَسْرُورُ
(A stranger who does not know him weeps over him, while his kinsman in the tribe is glad.)
And His saying: ﴿ذا مَتْرَبَةٍ﴾ [al-Balad: 16]: He means that, from his poverty, he has cleaved to the dust.

zajjaj:17-17.t: And His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ كانَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾: its meaning is: "When he did that, and had bound himself to faith, and then remained steadfast upon his faith." ﴿وَتَواصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ﴾ ("and enjoined one another to patience"): that is, upon obedience to Allah, and patience in refraining from entering into acts of disobedience to Him. Then, along with that, he was of those who enjoin one another to compassion; those are the people of good fortune (al-yumn) for themselves, that is, they were bringers of blessing upon themselves, not of ill omen.

zajjaj:19-19.t: ﴿والَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآياتِنا هم أصْحابُ المَشْأمَةِ﴾: that is, they are the bringers of ill omen upon themselves. We seek refuge in Allah from the Fire.

zajjaj:20-20.t: And His saying: ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ نارٌ مُؤْصَدَةٌ﴾ ("over them is a Fire closed in"): it is also read without hamza; its meaning is "closed over". One says ”آصَدْتُ البابَ“ and ”أوْصَدْتُهُ“ ("I closed the door") when I have shut it.
